items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: which was an old Bill Kenny tune from the Inkspots

ctx.x: I did an album in 1965 called “Ruth Brown ‘65” on Mainstream. The company went out of business. The record has been re-issued this year on SONY under a new name, it’s

now called “Softly.” And in that album I did “Here’s That Rainy Day,” I did “Why Do You Whisper Green Grass” which was an old Bill Kenny tune from the Inkspots, you know which dates back to my youth. And in that I also did “Porgy” — “I Love You Porgy.” Things that I had forgotten that I’d ever touched on. And I was listening to that album and I said, [whistles] I didn’t sound bad, you know? And then you go back and get some things like “Lucky Lips” and “This Little Girl’s Gone Rockin’” and “I Wrote My Momma a…
One last thing I would like to ask you. Who is coming up on the scene now as young R&B artists, that you think has their thumb on the pulse of great traditions.
